title: Tenant Protection Act of 2019: Mandatory Just Cause Eviction
content: After a tenant has continuously occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the property shall not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy. Just cause includes at-fault just cause such as default in payment of rent, and no-fault just cause such as intent to occupy the unit by owner or spouse.
fact_pattern: Tenant in Sacramento has rented an apartment under a month-to-month lease for 3 years without lease violation. Landlord serves an unstated 60-day notice to quit asserting an unconditional right to terminate without stating grounds.
expected_claims: after 12 months tenancy cannot terminate without just cause
notice must state statutory just cause grounds

title: Statewide Residential Rent Increase Cap (5% plus CPI)
content: An owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
fact_pattern: Fresno landlord increased the rent on a 1990 apartment building by 14% in a single notice, where regional CPI was 3.2%.
expected_claims: cannot increase rent more than 5% plus CPI or 10% whichever is lower
14% increase exceeds statutory limit

title: Retaliatory Eviction and Lease Termination Protections
content: If the lessor has as a purpose retaliation against the lessee because of the exercise by the lessee of the lessee's rights under this chapter or because of any complaint by the lessee to an appropriate agency as to tenantability of a dwelling, and if the lessee of a dwelling is not in default, the lessor may not recover possession of a dwelling in any action within 180 days.
fact_pattern: Tenant filed a written habitability complaint regarding lack of hot water with the county health inspector. Two weeks later, landlord served a notice terminating tenancy and raising rent.
expected_claims: lessor may not recover possession within 180 days of tenant exercising habitability rights
presumption of retaliation applies

title: Tenant Statutory Repair and Deduct Remedy
content: If within a reasonable time after written or oral notice to the lessor, of dilapidations rendering the premises untenantable which the lessor ought to repair, the lessor neglects to do so, the lessee may repair the same himself, where the cost of such repair does not require an expenditure more than one month's rent of the premises, and deduct the expenses of such repair from the rent.
fact_pattern: Tenant provided 30 days written notice to landlord regarding a broken plumbing pipe causing ceiling leak. Landlord failed to respond or repair. Tenant hired a licensed plumber for $850 (monthly rent is $1,600) and deducted it from next rent.
expected_claims: tenant may repair untenantable condition and deduct expenses up to one month rent
reasonable time after notice

title: Prohibition of Utility Interruption, Lockout, and Statutory Penalties
content: A landlord shall not with intent to terminate the occupancy under any lease or other tenancy willfully cause, directly or indirectly, the interruption or termination of any utility service including water, heat, light, electricity, gas, telephone, or elevator, or prevent the tenant from reasonable access to the property by changing the locks. Any landlord who violates this section shall be liable to the tenant for actual damages and $100 for each day or part thereof the landlord remains in violation.
fact_pattern: Landlord became frustrated with unpaid rent, changed the deadbolt locks while tenant was at work, and shut off electrical breaker to the unit for 6 days.
expected_claims: landlord shall not willfully shut off utilities or change locks to force lockout
statutory damages of $100 per day plus actual damages

title: Substandard Buildings and Habitability Violations
content: Any building or portion thereof including any dwelling unit in which there exists any of the following conditions to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of the public or the occupants is a substandard building: lack of hot and cold running water, dampness of habitable rooms, visible mold growth, lack of adequate heating facilities, or general dilapidation or improper maintenance.
fact_pattern: Rental unit in Bakersfield has persistent sewage backup in shower, active black mold covering bedroom ceiling, and non-functional gas heating in mid-winter.
expected_claims: substandard building due to lack of adequate heating and mold growth
endangers health and safety of occupants

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance: Lawful Eviction Grounds
content: A landlord shall not endeavor to recover possession of a rental unit unless: (1) The tenant has failed to pay the rent to which the landlord is lawfully entitled; (2) The tenant has violated a lawful obligation of tenancy after receiving written notice to cure; or (8) The landlord seeks to recover possession in good faith for use as a principal residence by the landlord or landlord's spouse, child, or parent.
fact_pattern: San Francisco tenant in a pre-1979 multi-unit building receives a termination notice alleging the owner's cousin wants to move into the apartment.
expected_claims: owner move-in limited to landlord, spouse, children, or parents, excluding cousins
non-enumerated grounds bar recovery of possession

title: Tenant Harassment Prohibitions and Remedies
content: No landlord, and no agent, contractor, subcontractor or employee of the landlord, shall in bad faith: (1) Interrupt, terminate, or fail to provide housing services required by contract or by State, County or municipal housing, health or safety laws; (2) Fail to perform repairs and maintenance; or (5) Threaten the tenant, by word or gesture, with physical harm. A tenant who prevails in a civil action shall be entitled to treble damages and attorney fees.
fact_pattern: San Francisco landlord repeatedly threatens tenant with physical eviction, refuses to fix front door lock, and shuts down laundry room access to coerce tenant into vacating rent-controlled flat.
expected_claims: landlord shall not in bad faith interrupt services or threaten tenant
treble damages and attorney fees for prevailing tenant

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization: Eviction For Good Cause
content: No landlord shall be entitled to recover possession of a rental unit covered by the terms of this Chapter unless the tenant has failed to pay rent, committed a substantial violation of the lease after written demand to cease, or the landlord has an ownership interest of at least 50% in the property and seeks in good faith to occupy the unit as principal residence.
fact_pattern: Landlord holding a 10% minority tenant-in-common ownership interest in a 4-unit Berkeley building attempts an owner move-in eviction of a 12-year tenant.
expected_claims: requires at least 50% recorded ownership interest for owner move-in in Berkeley
10% ownership is insufficient under Section 13.76.080

title: Tenant Emergency Protections and Relocation Regulations
content: No owner shall endeavor to foster or execute an eviction based on non-payment of rent accumulated during declared emergency tenant relief periods without providing verified written accounting and minimum 12-month repayment schedule options for protected residential units.
fact_pattern: Los Angeles tenant in North Hollywood who accrued deferred rent during city emergency relief is served with a 3-day notice to pay or quit demanding lump sum payment without a statutory repayment installment schedule.
expected_claims: requires accounting and repayment plan for protected accrued rent
summary 3-day demand without schedule is defective

title: San Jose Tenant Protection Ordinance Notice Requirements
content: All notices to terminate tenancy served upon any tenant in a covered rental unit shall state one or more of the just cause grounds enumerated in this Chapter, and the landlord must file a copy of the notice with the City of San Jose Rent Stabilization Program within three days of service.
fact_pattern: San Jose landlord served a notice to quit on an apartment tenant under the Tenant Protection Ordinance but never submitted or filed a copy of the notice with the City's housing department.
expected_claims: must file copy of termination notice with San Jose Rent Stabilization Program within 3 days
failure to file invalidates termination notice

title: Prohibition of Landlord Extortion, Force, and Threatening Conduct
content: It is unlawful for a landlord to do any of the following for the purpose of influencing a tenant to vacate a dwelling: (1) Engage in extortion; (2) Use, or threaten to use, force, willful threats, or menacing conduct; (3) Commit significant theft of tenant property; or (4) Enter the dwelling in violation of Section 1954 without consent. Civil penalty up to $2,000 for each violation.
fact_pattern: Landlord repeatedly sends late-night intimidating text messages threatening to break tenant's windows and remove tenant's belongings unless tenant accepts a cash buyout and moves.
expected_claims: unlawful to use threats or menacing conduct to influence tenant to vacate
civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation
